# Phase 6 handoff — blocked candidate

Status: **BLOCKED**. No Phase 6 release or Phase 7 authorization is claimed.

## Repository state and delivery

The last verified committed state is Phase 5 delivery
`03c32df5c2d5edcb4606564d1dba215d26640116`, with ancestry
`e040229ad4e363a833f9dc74b414cdb2217cf664` →
`caffc0beeff15b35370c03c834f884cbf9407e26` →
`b7a152709d82e614b0c1ff0e25432218360a7504` → that delivery.
The dedicated working branch is `codex/phase6-interrupts-exceptions`.
No Phase 6 implementation commit or push has been made: the project permits
committing only verified states, and architectural approval remains withheld.
The candidate is retained for review, not discarded or hidden by cleanup.
Remote inspection confirms the Phase 5 branch still names that delivery and no
Phase 6 work branch has been published. There is consequently no Phase 6 remote
SHA or CI run to claim. An unauthenticated GitHub Actions API read returned 404;
it supplies no independent CI evidence.

## Actual blocker and recovery

The [independent review](PHASE6_ARCHITECTURAL_REVIEW.md) records three required
286-specific decisions not resolved by the available primary/physical evidence:

1. Whether an IRET attempt that faults releases NMI inhibition.
2. Whether STI creates its shadow when old IF=1, including repeated STI.
3. Whether a faulting instruction with sampled TF triggers #1 after delivery,
   given contradictory manual passages.

The candidate's policies are explicit and its directed tests characterize them.
Model agreement is not physical adjudication. The independent model refuses to
invent a failed-IRET/NMI oracle. Primary manuals, the B-2/B-3 sheet, corpus
methodology and the examined physical-report collection did not settle these
distinctions; no physical 286 fixture is connected here. The review gives exact
discriminating captures and controls. Obtain those captures or an explicit Intel
286 clarification, adjudicate each policy, update RTL/models only from evidence,
rerun the complete fresh gate, and request a refreshed independent review.

`docs/phase6_evidence.json` prevents the release gate from emitting
`PHASE6_VALIDATION_PASS` while these findings remain unresolved. There is no
engineering-only switch that labels an incomplete architecture ready.

## Candidate implementation

Shared generated event entry handles software INT3/INT imm8/INTO, supported
#UD/#GP producers, sampled TF, NMI and INTR. Supporting forms are IRET,
PUSHF/POPF, CLI/STI and HLT. Event selection and saved start/next context remain
separate from functional microcode; existing architectural state, segment,
stack, operand, fetch and BIU owners are reused.

The BIU owns both READY-qualified INTA cycles, samples only the second low byte,
and retains LOCK through the first completed frame word. HOLD/HLDA cannot split
that chain or a logical odd word. Entry and IRET stage context and use the normal
CS/cache/IP redirect protocol. Accepted writes and completed SP effects are not
rolled back. Shutdown differs from halt and retains documented partial effects.

All 1,423 formerly excluded inherited nonprefixed exceptions are admitted.
Physical 8F destination-limit cases corrected an inherited precheck assumption:
the completed POP advances SP before destination #GP. Invalid 8F groups deliver
#UD immediately at ModR/M; arbitrary initialized capture-tail bytes are not
misdecoded as required operands. Legal unsupported forms remain explicit.

Compiler 5.0 / format 5 has 28 entries, 128 words, seven-bit addresses and six-bit
controls. Frozen formats 1–4 and the independent active contract remain tested.
Generated artifacts are source-derived; no handwritten ROM modifications occur.

Existing non-event streaming benches now seed TF clear so that their intended
ALU/MOV/stack streams execute without entering unrelated handlers. TF set/clear,
sampling and competition are exercised in the new event suites. Older limit
benches pause at the real fault producer to inspect pre-delivery suppression;
the admitted full exception corpus and new event suites verify actual delivery.
No physical expected register/memory values were changed to accommodate RTL.

## Trace and architectural review findings

Eleven pristine hardware replays plus the directed INTA/HOLD trace are extracted
by `tools.inspect_event_traces`. INT3 writes FLAGS, CS and next IP before IVT
reads; IRET performs three ordered reads before one coherent context/retirement;
#UD/#GP complete events without retirement. The odd #GP frame splits each word
into the correct two lanes. The INTR trace shows first low byte 99 ignored,
second low byte 42 selected, LOCK through both halves of the first frame word,
and HOLD granted only after that word. Trace timestamps are simulator coordinates,
not historical 80286 timing measurements.

The independent reviewer reproduced a pause-dependent defect after CLI at
CS:FFFF with TF=1: a next-opcode #GP could displace a previously owed #1.
Arbitration now distinguishes active-instruction faults from new opcode demand;
both uninterrupted and paused executions deliver #1 with saved IP=0000.
The refreshed review closed that defect and the model/coverage findings, found
no additional concrete RTL defect within its bounded inspection, and withheld
architectural approval for the three evidence questions above.

## Scope and limitations

This remains an unprefixed 16-bit Real Mode CPU candidate. Protected mode,
general prefixes, later instruction families, 80287, variable IDTR/gates,
machine/chipset integration and Accurate/Fast/Max profiles are deferred.
No cycle-accurate native pin timing, FPGA ALM count or Fmax is claimed. Corpus
functional passes and parser cycle agreement do not establish RTL cycle equality.
TF/NMI/INTR concurrency, READY perturbations and low-SP entry failures rely on
directed evidence because the pinned hardware corpus does not exercise them.

## Validated provisional development baseline — 2026-09-08

The fresh `build/phase7-baseline-2` run completed `make phase6-exec-check`
with Linux exit status 0. It emitted `PHASE6_EXECUTABLE_VALIDATION_PASS`;
it did not emit strict architectural approval. The input manifest was
rechecked at completion (158 executable validation files).

The unchanged three evidence IDs remain pending: `failed-iret-nmi`,
`sti-old-if`, and `fault-tf`. The original review remains approval-withheld.

- Original HEAD: `03c32df5c2d5edcb4606564d1dba215d26640116`.
- Original staged tree: `94fcf66a13ca6a1d618feeff37a48c886d37aa86`.
- Original combined recovery tree: `5938abf0c2f68cb26f71da294bc2c4606c1d26b7`.
- Both original recovery package manifests and archive hashes were verified;
  no recovery archive was applied over the combined working candidate.
- Full preserved cohort: 474,049 passed, zero failed, 106 families.
- Original compiler/ROM audits, both simulators, event streams/lifecycle,
  physical/parser/comparator audits, inherited/event mutations, failure
  propagation, trace checks, Yosys synthesis and final regression passed
  through the shared executable gate.
- Run log SHA-256:
  `f36c113625fecfcc00174cc51aaf6f6076a41e6ce20416e754272e158d36598c`.
- Reproduction: choose a previously absent absolute build directory and run
  `SPK286_BUILD_DIR=... make phase6-exec-check` from WSL Ubuntu 24.04.

The earlier `build/phase7-baseline` run was deliberately interrupted
(Linux make status -15) to fix CI pipeline error propagation before validation.
It is retained as an interrupted attempt, never counted as a pass.

Phase 7 implementation and review remain incomplete. Its isolated prototype
and physical inventory are not part of this baseline's executable claims.

against its exact remote tip. GitHub Actions

completed with conclusion `success`, verified on 2026-09-08. Its explicit
architectural status remains pending for the same three questions. The current
